Minesweeper Cheat Sheet

Rules, deductions, patterns, controls, and a final check before you guess.

Play MinesweeperPattern ExamplesStrategy Guide

What the numbers mean

A number counts mines in all eight surrounding squares, including diagonals.

1one mine
2two mines
3three mines
4+four or more

Goal

Reveal every safe square. Flags are notes for proven mines; they do not need to be placed to win.

The two core deductions

Safe rule: If a clue already touches its required number of flags, every other covered neighbor is safe.

Mine rule: If the number of unflagged covered neighbors equals the mines still required, all those neighbors are mines.

Recount flags before using either rule. A wrong flag creates wrong deductions.

Common patterns

1-2-1In the standard three-cell strip, outer candidates are mines and the middle is safe.
1-2-2-1In the standard four-cell strip, middle candidates are mines and outer candidates are safe.
2-1 edgeThe candidate seen only by the 2 is a mine; subtract it from the shared group.
1-1-1Usually not enough by itself. Find another clue before acting.

Patterns can rotate or mirror. Use them only when the covered-neighbor sets match the full example.

Set subtraction

  1. List the covered neighbors of two nearby clues.
  2. Remove the candidates they share.
  3. Subtract the smaller remaining mine requirement.
  4. Use the difference to prove the extra squares safe or mined.

This is the logic behind many visual patterns.

Before you guess

  1. Scan every open boundary, not only the stuck area.
  2. Recheck flags and diagonal neighbors.
  3. Compare overlapping clue sets.
  4. Use the remaining mine counter.
  5. Ask whether another area can reveal more information.

Only estimate probability when no certain move remains. Read the 50/50 guide for true ambiguous positions.

Controls and safe speed

Desktop: left click to reveal, right click to flag, and click an open number to chord when its flags are verified.

Mobile: switch between Reveal and Flag modes. Large boards can scroll horizontally.

Keyboard: arrow keys move, Enter or Space reveals, and F flags on Endlessweep.

Speed comes from fewer unnecessary actions, not from skipping verification.

Keep this sheet nearby, then practice each deduction on a real board.
